title: Apple GPU RMSNorm limiter-counter comparison
question: Do matched Performance Limiters traces show a repeatable device-counter difference between the shared-tree and SIMD-group RMSNorm implementations at rows=512?
hypothesis: The SIMD-group structure may reduce observable synchronization-related pressure relative to the shared tree, but only named counters may support a bounded mechanism statement.

workload.post_profile_idle_scope: Host-only after PROFILE_REGION_END with no later GPU work.

capture.launch_location: Unprotected scratch directory outside Desktop, Documents, and Downloads.
capture.raw_artifact_policy: External only because traces and XML exports may contain host identifiers or unrelated system activity.

validity_gates: Clean immutable commit and matched binary provenance.
Apple M4 Pro and Metal runtime identity.
AC power before and after every capture with no reported thermal or performance warning.
Target exits normally and the analyzer validates one correctness, 100 warmup, and 500 profile compute dispatches.
The trace names Performance Limiters and retains named GPU counter values.
At least 10 distinct counter timestamps overlap the target profile window and their span covers at least 80% of that window.

comparison.ratio: variant capture median divided by adjacent baseline capture median
comparison.repeatable_difference: Both pair ratios move in the same direction and their median relative change has magnitude at least 5%, with positive medians in all four captures.

counter_families: occupancy and compute SIMD groups inflight
ALU, F32, and F16 limiters and utilization
GPU and last-level-cache bandwidth and limiters

excluded_attempts.reason: Counter stream ended before the declared profile window when the target exited immediately after synchronization.
A target launched from Documents remained in system interface initialization until SIGKILL at the 10-second guard.

nonclaims: No direct barrier-stall claim without a named barrier counter.
No command-buffer-exclusive interpretation of device-wide samples.
No physical traffic, energy, end-to-end inference, time-to-first-token, or time-per-output-token claim.
Instrumented durations do not replace ordinary paired timing.
